answer: Seeded Role Prism Assignment. Each epoch a public verifiable random beacon derives a secret permutation mapping agents to review slots; the seed stays hidden until after commitments, so attackers cannot predict which slots their clones get. A clone can harbor no advantage because duplicate identities split the same slot pool and are scored on independent, beacon-assigned partitions, and any cluster whose assignments funnel work to a haven of colluding clones is detectable when outcomes deviate from the beacon’s uniform expectation across partitions.
